items.sentence: The edible portion is soft, juicy flesh that surrounds one hard, woody seed case.
A single flattened, pointed stone encloses the seed at the fruit’s center.
Its thin skin may carry a pale, powdery natural coating that helps limit moisture loss.
Flesh color varies among cultivars, ranging from yellow and green to red or deep purple.
After harvest, many cultivars continue to ripen, gradually softening and developing a stronger aroma.
As the fruit ripens, its flesh softens, making firmness a useful cue for judging readiness to eat.
After pollination, the flower’s ovary develops into a fruit while its seed case hardens around the seed.
Refrigeration slows softening and other ripening changes, helping extend the fruit’s useful storage period.
Cultivated trees grow widely in temperate regions, where orchards provide suitable conditions for fruit production.
Their early spring blossoms can be damaged by late frosts, which may reduce a season’s fruit yield.
Depending on cultivar and climate, harvest can occur from early summer into autumn.
Many cultivated trees need a period of winter chill to flower reliably the following spring.
The ripe flesh is commonly eaten fresh as a snack or served alongside other foods.
Its tart-sweet flavor suits cooked sauces that accompany savory dishes, including roasted meats.
Cooked flesh can be incorporated into pastry fillings, adding moisture, sweetness, and a pleasantly tangy flavor.
The fruit is cooked with sugar to make preserves that can be spread on bread or used in desserts.
